collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — BELIEF, IDENTITY AND PERSONAL EXPRESSION (BLF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Religious, spiritual, atheist, agnostic, questioning and simply uninterested villagers living side by side; who people are, whom they love and how they present themselves. Privacy is respected, nobody has to explain or justify anything, and differences don't have to be the subject. Gods and spirits stay unconfirmed either way.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: Someone at the fire asks a villager what they believe, in front of everyone: give a joke answer, or say it is private.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the fire tonight, someone asks (subject), "So what do YOU believe in, then?" Everyone turns to look. (subject) has never talked about it. (subject.He/she) isn't sure (subject.he/she) wants to start now, in front of everyone, with a mouthful of fish.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) swallows (subject.his/her) fish. "Right now," (subject.he/she) says, "I believe this is very good fish." Everyone laughs. The conversation moves on. Later, walking home, (friend) asks quietly, "Do you really not want to say?" "Not at the fire," says (subject). "Maybe sometime. Maybe not." (friend) nods. "That's fair."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "I'd rather not say," says (subject) pleasantly. "It's private." There's a little pause. Then (friend) says, "That's fair. Who wants more fish?" And that's the end of it. (subject) is grateful to (friend) for the rest of the evening. It's easy to forget how much one sentence can help.
